name: dive
summary: Tool for exploring Docker image layers and finding ways to shrink size.
use_cases: explore Docker image contents broken down by layer
estimate image efficiency and wasted space
features: show Docker image contents by layer
indicate what changed in each layer
estimate image efficiency and wasted space

steps.command:
DIVE_VERSION=0.13.1
curl -fL "https://github.com/wagoodman/dive/releases/download/v${DIVE_VERSION}/dive_${DIVE_VERSION}_linux_amd64.tar.gz" -o /tmp/dive.tar.gz
mkdir -p ~/.local/bin
tar -xzf /tmp/dive.tar.gz -C /tmp && mv /tmp/dive ~/.local/bin/dive && chmod +x ~/.local/bin/dive && ~/.local/bin/dive --version

setup.command:
cat > /tmp/make_archive.py <<'PYEOF'
import tarfile, json, os, io, tempfile, hashlib

tmpdir = "/tmp/dive-image"
os.makedirs(tmpdir, exist_ok=True)

# Create two layers to test layer diff
# Layer 1: contains /hello.txt
# Layer 2: adds /world.txt and modifies /hello.txt

def make_layer_tar(files, path):
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    with tarfile.open(fileobj=buf, mode='w') as tf:
        for name, content in files.items():
            data = content.encode()
            ti = tarfile.TarInfo(name=name)
            ti.size = len(data)
            ti.mtime = 0
            tf.addfile(ti, io.BytesIO(data))
    data = buf.getvalue()
    with open(path, 'wb') as f:
        f.write(data)
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()

layer1_hash = make_layer_tar({"hello.txt": "hello from layer1\n"}, "/tmp/dive-image/layer1.tar")
layer2_hash = make_layer_tar({"world.txt": "hello world\n", "hello.txt": "modified hello\n"}, "/tmp/dive-image/layer2.tar")

# Create config json
config = {
    "architecture": "amd64",
    "os": "linux",
    "rootfs": {"type": "layers", "diff_ids": [f"sha256:{layer1_hash}", f"sha256:{layer2_hash}"]},
    "history": [{"created": "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"}, {"created": "2025-01-02T00:00:00Z"}],
    "config": {}
}
import hashlib as hl
config_data = json.dumps(config).encode()
config_hash = hl.sha256(config_data).hexdigest()

with open(f"/tmp/dive-image/{config_hash}.json", "wb") as f:
    f.write(config_data)

# manifest.json
manifest = [{
    "Config": f"{config_hash}.json",
    "RepoTags": ["test:latest"],
    "Layers": ["layer1.tar", "layer2.tar"]
}]
with open("/tmp/dive-image/manifest.json", "w") as f:
    json.dump(manifest, f)

with open("/tmp/dive-image/repositories", "w") as f:
    json.dump({"test": {"latest": "layer2"}}, f)

# Create docker save tarball
with tarfile.open("/tmp/test-image.tar", "w") as out:
    for fname in ["manifest.json", "repositories", f"{config_hash}.json", "layer1.tar", "layer2.tar"]:
        out.add(f"/tmp/dive-image/{fname}", arcname=fname)

print(f"Created /tmp/test-image.tar with layers {layer1_hash[:12]}, {layer2_hash[:12]}, config {config_hash[:12]}")
print(f"Size: {os.path.getsize('/tmp/test-image.tar')}")

PYEOF
python3 /tmp/make_archive.py
tar -tvf /tmp/test-image.tar

pitfalls.readme_said: Install via go install or pacman -S dive (and brew/docker)
pitfalls.actually_needed: On Debian without Go/Docker, downloaded prebuilt linux_amd64 tarball from GitHub releases and extracted to ~/.local/bin

pitfalls.readme_said: dive nginx:latest uses Docker daemon by default
pitfalls.actually_needed: Used --source docker-archive with a crafted docker save tarball to test without Docker daemon; registry source not available in v0.13.1
dive build requires docker client executable; fails gracefully when absent
